A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cell-MNN work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including the rasterized appendix figures in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original single-cell interpolation, amortized training, scaling, TRRUST validation, and eigenvalue-ablation results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds GRN comparisons, interaction-existence evaluation, PCA diagnostics, and higher-dimensional interpolation experiments.

M1.justification: The PCA projection, MLP-predicted local operator, eigendecomposition, analytical decoding, loss terms, and optional zero-eigenvalue variant are retained. The additional evaluation procedures and dimensional configurations do not establish a change to the proposed Cell-MNN algorithm.

E1.justification: EB, Cite, Multi, and TRRUST remain the data sources. Appendix F.1 adds prediction of interaction existence beyond classifying the signs of known interactions, while Appendix E adds cell-type classification diagnostics. These provide a focused task expansion; the higher PCA dimensions change settings rather than biological dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v1's gene-interaction evaluation compared Cell-MNN variants with guessing. v2 adds SCODE and OT-CFM Jacobians to the signed-interaction comparison in Table 2, and GRNBoost2, SCODE, and OT-CFM Jacobians to the new existence evaluation in Table 9. Table 11 also introduces WLF-SB and WLF-OT comparisons. This substantially strengthens comparator coverage.

E3.justification: The original experimental protocols remain, but v2 adds substantial new settings: 10D interpolation and 50D/100D experiments with unwhitened PCA, global rescaling, different learning rates, batch size 1028, and revised stopping patience. Appendix F.1 introduces a 70-regulator candidate set with 447 reference interactions and AUROC/Enrichment@500 evaluation; Appendix E adds k-nearest-neighbor classification with k=15.

E4.justification: v2 adds explained-variance analysis, cell-type UMAPs, and classification diagnostics to assess information retained by 5D PCA, plus experiments testing sensitivity to 10, 50, and 100 dimensions. These substantially broaden validation of the representation choice. The earlier zero-eigenvalue ablations and appendix operator visualizations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Table 1 removes standard deviations from the across-dataset Average column; for example, Cell-MNN's 0.741 ± 0.050 becomes 0.741. Per-dataset uncertainty remains. Both versions already specify three random seeds, so the new reproducibility statement and seed-based result tables do not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: The retained interpolation, scaling, amortization, and eigenvalue-ablation means are unchanged. New Table 2 reports average signed-interaction F1 of 69% for Cell-MNN versus 46% for SCODE and 48% for OT-CFM(J). Table 9 adds Cell-MNN AUROC 0.659 and Enrichment@500 18.572, without leading both metrics. Tables 10–11 add mixed-ranking higher-dimensional results, and Appendix E reports cell-type accuracies of 87% for Multi and 90% for Cite.

T1.justification: The main equations and Appendix D's ODE-factorization proposition and proof are unchanged. v2 adds the normalized definition of Enrichment@K in Appendix F.1 and an EMD homogeneity argument justifying conversion of rescaled evaluation scores back to original PCA units in Appendix G.1.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction drop the explicit assertion that learned interactions are biologically consistent, emphasizing interpretability and TRRUST validation instead. This modestly qualifies the headline biological claim. The five stated contributions and the main interpolation, scalability, and amortization claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly scopes the contribution as improving dynamics given a standard embedding. Appendix F.1 qualifies the global GRN evaluation because averaging discards context and signs, and restricting GRNBoost2's regulators supplies prior information. Appendix G.1 explains the memory benefit of fewer analytical decoding points. The existing local-linearity and TRRUST-context limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated reproducibility statement with repository and data-access information, environment.yml, and README reproduction instructions, beyond v1's existing hyperparameter disclosures. Appendix G.1 documents normalization, an L40S GPU, dimensionality-specific settings, runtimes, and memory use; Appendix F.1 specifies operator aggregation for the new evaluation.

R1.justification: v2 adds SCODE and discusses time-resolved GRN methods Dynamo, SCENIC+, Marlene, and Dictys, distinguishing their input requirements from Cell-MNN's use of standard expression counts. This is a focused expansion of GRN positioning. The broader interpolation and ODE-discovery positioning remains, while bibliographic and citation-style updates do not represent new research.

P1.justification: Most methodological prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 makes targeted abstract and results rewrites, expands related work, adds a reproducibility section and appendix subsections, and reorganizes the closing statements. These are localized narrative changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds the multipanel PCA Figure 7 and Tables 2 and 9–11, revises Figure 1's labels, and adopts ICLR typography, headers, and substantially reflowed figure/table placement. Table 1 explicitly labels the 5D settings. The original appendix UMAP panels remain, renumbered as Figures 8–11, rather than constituting new visual analyses.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses two weaknesses in v1: biological validation without learned GRN comparators and evaluation restricted to 5D embeddings. Tables 2 and 9–11 and Appendix E provide meaningful comparative and representation checks, including mixed outcomes that better establish applicability boundaries. Added reproduction instructions improve transparency. The loss of Table 1's average-column uncertainty is a limited reporting drawback, outweighed by the stronger validation.
